newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas lower in West, firmer in East.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas lower in West, firmer in East.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were lower in the West but slightly stronger in the East Monday, driven by differing weather patterns, sources said.
At the AECO storage hub, prices for Tuesday delivery ranged anywhere from C$3.75 early to C$3.01 per gigajoule (GJ) late.
Traders said most deals were done in the high-C$3.20s, down about 50 cents from Friday, as milder air moved into western Canada and the start of February neared.
Temperatures in Calgary are forecast to reach zero by Thursday, sources said.
"The January market has to start converging with February," noting prices at AECO for next month were in the C$2.80-2.90 per GJ range.
At Sumas, Wash., prices softened by about two cents to an average range of $2.84-2.89 per million British thermal units (mmBtu).
Traders reported closing deals anywhere from $2.60 to $3.00 per mmBtu.
At Niagara, prices rose by about five cents to the $3.15-3.20 per mmBtu range, as the expiring February Henry Hub NYMEX gas contract jumped to a high of $3.06.
